newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's PLA team in HK collects mystery boxes.
newsitem.headline: China's PLA team in HK collects mystery boxes.

text.p: Troops of China's People's Liberation Army visited a Bank of China building in Hong Kong on Monday and emerged with a stack of metal boxes about the right size to contain weapons, eyewitnesses said.
An officer in the group manhandled an American news photographer who happened to be at the scene when he attempted to photograph the PLA's visit.

A diplomat close to Sino-British negotiations on Hong Kong's handover to China -- now just a week away -- said a PLA honour guard was preparing for handover ceremonies and might have been collecting parade weapons from a Chinese company office.
"I saw 25 to 35 PLA men, all looking superhumanly over six feet tall, wearing PLA trousers and PLA buckles, and in golf shirts," said Mike Wilbur, an American photographer.
"They carried out six to ten aluminium boxes measuring about five feet by two by two and loaded them on to buses," Wilbur told Reuters.
The photographer, working on the handover for the Far Eastern Economic Review magazine, said a PLA officer pounced on him when he raised his camera to shoot the mysterious operation.
"When I tried to take a picture, the officer became completely uncorked and physically prevented me from taking a picture," Wilbur said.
"They said it was against the law and I needed permission."
The action took place at a Bank of China branch in the heart of the Wanchai commercial district, near the venue of the handover party, the Hong Kong Convention Centre.
It is also not far from the Prince of Wales Barracks, where the leading group of a 196-strong PLA advance party preparing future garrison facilities is based.

A spokesman at the Bank of China said he knew nothing about the visit by the PLA men. A spokesman for the British armed forces denied all knowledge of the incident. A spokesman for the government's Security Branch declined to comment without proof that the men were Chinese troops.
And there was no comment from the PLA itself. The PLA keeps its telephone number at the Prince of Wales Barracks secret, and British officers refuse to divulge it.
However, a senior diplomat close to the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group talks said it was quite possible that the men were the PLA honour guard collecting presentation weapons.
"The PLA advance guard are not allowed to bear arms and as far as we know they have none," the diplomat said.
"But there are 36 men in the honour guard and they are practising these days for the ceremonies, so they may have weapons for presentation purposes only," he said.

A flashy Sino-British ceremony including honour guards from both sides will take place at midnight on June 30, when Britain's Prince Charles will formally hand back Hong Kong to China's President Jiang Zemin, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
